Variants.Content: Blackwater Bay takes over the Blackwater and flows into the Narrow Sea. King's Landing is built on the north bank of the river mouth. Dragonstone and many small islands guard the road to the outer sea. A large amount of grain, firewood and cargo arrived in the capital through the docks in the bay, and the royal fleet shared anchorage, tidal channels and pilotage needs with merchant ships. If the enemy controls the mouth of the bay, it can threaten supplies and landings; if the defender blocks the river, it must also be responsible for crowded ships, fire attacks, and wind direction. The Battle of the Blackwater makes wildfires and burning ships one of the bay's most horrific memories, but even without the war, siltation, smuggling and delays to grain ships would have been enough to unsettle King's Landing.

King's Landing Dockers judge whether prices will rise in town based on the number of sails and draft. While the throne room continues to debate, a few less grain ships are enough to line up Flea Bottom.

Both the king and the Dragonstone generals regard Blackwater Bay as the key to the capital. If the fleet is unfamiliar with tides and river mouths, no matter how many ships there are, they may hinder each other in narrow water.

Outsiders can easily see the Red Fort and wealth from the bay, but those who have experienced the fire battle will remember how the green flames illuminated the entire water. The calmness of the bay has always been a bit unbelievable.
